`abstract class UIBridge`<br/>
**Implements:** [`IUIBridge`](/reference/backends/iuibridge/)<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`StackUIBridge`](/reference/backends/stackuibridge/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.bridge.ui` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [UIBridge.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/bridge/ui/UIBridge.java)

The base class of every UI bridge, which dispatches the input to its UIs, updates them and draws them by layer.

## Description

A subclass decides what opening and closing a UI mean; [`StackUIBridge`](/reference/backends/stackuibridge/) already does it with a screen stack, and is the usual base.
[`UIBridgeRegistry`](/reference/backends/uibridgeregistry/) calls the input methods and the steps of the frame; each input method returns `true` when the bridge consumed the event.
This bridge overrides `drawBackground()` to keep the scene of the host under its UIs:

```java file="com/example/running/SceneUIBridge.java"
```

<a id="UIBridge-method-draw"></a>

### draw

`void draw()` 

Draws every UI of the bridge; the same as `draw(filter)` with a filter that accepts every UI.

`void draw(Predicate<UI> filter)` 

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: ….draw() needs an open frame and the render bridge has none: call render.beginFrame() before and render.endFrame() after, or use BridgeHandler.UI.frame()

Draws the shown UIs that the filter accepts: the overlays below the screens, then the screens and popups, then the overlays above the screens, each group in `zindex` order, then sets the cursor.
It first releases the GPU resources that nothing uses any more.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` outside a frame of the render bridge; a draw that throws skips the rest of the frame of the bridge, puts the matrix and state stacks back and prints one warning.

<a id="UIBridge-method-isScreenOpen"></a>

### isScreenOpen

`boolean isScreenOpen()` 

If `true`, the bridge holds a UI that is not an overlay.
JOID never calls it: a host overrides it to answer for its own screens too.

<a id="UIBridge-method-isOverlayHidden"></a>

### isOverlayHidden

`boolean isOverlayHidden()` 

If `true`, the overlays that do not ask to stay drawn are neither drawn nor given the input; `false` by default.
Override it to follow a host that hides its own interface.

<a id="UIBridge-method-drawBackground"></a>

### drawBackground

`void drawBackground()` <span class="joid-qualifier">hook</span> <span class="joid-qualifier">protected</span>

JOID calls it once per frame on the bridge of the lowest priority only, before any UI is drawn; it does nothing by default.
Override it to clear or paint the window.
